replication.target_description: Attitudes main effect: factor unspecified, so source-expertise and source-certainty main effects are both candidates.

notes: Identity verified in supplied canonical excerpt: title Uncertainty, expertise, and persuasion: A replication and extension of Karmarkar and Tormala (2010), authors Erik Løhre, Subramanya Prasad Chandrashekar, Lewend Mayiwar, Thorvald Hærem, JESP 113 (2024) 104619, DOI 10.1016/j.jesp.2024.104619 (p. 1, L0–L64). Published primary empirical Registered Report with actual Results, not a preregistration. Cache contains PDF-derived web excerpts (L0–371 and L488–896), not the complete 13-page paper. No local PDF supplied; no acquisition performed. Only assigned replication fields assessed. Certainty main effect: F(1, 506) = 4.27, p = .039, partial η² = 0.01. Expertise main effect: F(1, 506) = 1.35, p = .247, partial η² = 0.00. No factor selected by row order or numeric matching. Common model N candidate only: 257 high-certainty participants + 253 low-certainty participants = 510 participants. These are mutually exclusive final certainty groups within the direct-replication 2 × 2 model, not the whole-study recruitment N = 1018. No N was inferred from degrees of freedom.
